=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- Requirement: "Revalidate the head and base in the merge helper, and enforce the reviewed head/base pair at merge time; automatically cancel authorization and trigger re-review on retarget." (Linked issue #5905)
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py:evaluate, when the marker's base binding no longer matches the PR's current base on a later sweep tick
  Evidence of absence: The implementation catches a retarget within the sweep's own window: the post-enable re-read at lines 742-768 revokes auto-merge on a moved pair. However, a retarget that happens after post-enable read succeeds (pair held, merge_enabled returned) while auto-merge remains pending is not caught. The next sweep tick finds the marker no longer matches the current base and returns base_changed at lines 678-681 without calling revoke_auto_merge, so the stale auto-merge authorization from the earlier sweep run persists. The plan AD-2 accepts this gap for write-access users (they can merge directly) and relies on GitHub's own auto-merge disable for non-write retargets, but the linked issue does not distinguish these cases and unconditionally requires cancelling authorization on retarget.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

The code, tests, docstrings, README, and agents.md all name it correctly; only this one static description is stale.

The implementation in scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py:108 declares `PENDING_CHECKS_ALARM_STATES = ("merge_revoke_failed", "merge_revoke_unconfirmed", "merged_unreviewed_base")` and the warning block at scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py:288-292 emits the ::warning:: for all three; tests/test_claude_fixer_pending_checks.py:1396-1401 also asserts all three trigger warnings. The phase-description list, however, omits `merge_revoke_unconfirmed`. AD-7 was recorded after the phase list was written, and the docs/implement-plan log is the static deliverable the §11 checklist reads against.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- TASK_GAP_2
  Requirement: From the linked issue's Recommendation: "Revalidate the head and base in the merge helper, and enforce the reviewed head/base pair at merge time; automatically cancel authorization and trigger re-review on retarget." The in-sweep retarget window is closed; the broader concern — automatically cancelling the authorization after the sweep has already returned merge_enabled — is the residual case the issue's recommendation calls out.
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py::evaluate, the auto_merge early-return at lines 678-681
  Evidence of absence: evaluate() checks `pr.get("auto_merge")` at line 678 and returns {"state": "not_eligible", ...} at line 681 BEFORE any of the new revoke helpers (enable_auto_merge with REVIEWED_BASE_*, recheck_reviewed_pair, revoke_auto_merge) can run. Concretely: after the first sweep run calls `gh pr merge --auto` and returns merge_enabled, every subsequent sweep run on the same PR sees `auto_merge=True` and exits at line 681 with not_eligible — the new revoke code at lines 732-768 is never reached. internal-review.yml:11-12 listens for `pull_request: types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, closed]` and does NOT include `edited`, so a write-capable retarget (the issue's exploit) does not trigger any review workflow run to dispatch the gate; the claude-pr-catch-all sweep only dispatches for due conflict/CI/review/block fixes, not for stale-marker retargets. The PR therefore retains its auto-merge authorization on the unreviewed base until either a push fires pull_request:synchronize (an unrelated event) or the merge itself lands. The plan accepts this as residual risk in the Risks section, but the linked issue's recommendation does not defer it, and §10/§1 of CLAUDE.md and the security-finding severity (high, 9/10) put the cancellation requirement on the implementation. AD-2 alternative B was rejected; the live code path implements alternative A only.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

Line 20 says the sweep "warns on `merge_revoke_failed` / `merged_unreviewed_base`" but omits `merge_revoke_unconfirmed`. The code at `scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py:108` includes it in `PENDING_CHECKS_ALARM_STATES`, the warning block at lines 288-292 covers all three states, the test at lines 1396-1401 asserts it, and README/agents.md mention all three. The omission is a doc lag: AD-7 was recorded after the phase description was written.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- DISAGREEMENT: The finding claims a retarget after the post-enable re-read (which returned `merge_enabled`) is not caught because a later `evaluate` run returns `not_eligible` at lines 678-681 (`auto_merge` already enabled) before reaching the base-binding check. This is a real code path, but the plan explicitly accepts it as a residual risk in AD-2 and Risks & Mitigations: "A retarget by a user with write access after the post-enable re-read while auto-merge is still pending. ACCEPTED: that user can merge the PR directly under the same protection, and GitHub disables auto-merge for a retarget by anyone without write access." The linked issue's "automatically cancel authorization and trigger re-review on retarget" is satisfied for the window the sweep itself opens (between evaluate's first read and the post-enable read); the post-enable window is an accepted residual with a documented rationale (§28 auto-decision AD-2). Re-flagging an explicitly accepted residual without new evidence from LAST RUN DIFF is not warranted — the review-round-1 change (confirming read) narrows the window further rather than widening it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
